paragraphs: Throughout this Annual Report on Form 10-K, except as otherwise noted by the context, the terms "DuPont" or "Company" used herein mean DuPont de Nemours, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.

DuPont is a leading provider of advanced solutions that improve everyday life across healthcare, water, construction and industrial markets. The Company is committed to helping customers advance their technology pipelines and provide solutions that address their unique challenges. From delivering clean water to enabling medical packaging solutions which enhance safety and performance, DuPont's innovations power the essential products and technologies people rely on every day. At December 31, 2025, the Company has subsidiaries in about 50 countries worldwide and manufacturing operations in about 20 countries. See Note 23 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for details on the location of the Company's sales and property.

DuPont is a Delaware corporation formed in 2015 (formerly, DowDuPont Inc.), for the purpose of effecting the all-stock merger of equals transactions between The Dow Chemical Company ("TDCC") and E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company (n/k/a as EIDP, Inc., "EIDP"), which became effective on August 31, 2017. As a result of the merger, TDCC and EIDP became subsidiaries of DowDuPont Inc. (the "DWDP Merger"). The DWDP Merger aimed to combine the strengths of both companies and then realign the assets to create three more focused and streamlined public companies.

On April 1, 2019, the Company completed the separation of the materials science business through the spin-off of Dow Inc., ("Dow") including Dow's subsidiary TDCC (the "Dow Distribution"). On June 1, 2019, the Company completed the separation of the agriculture business through the spin-off of Corteva, Inc. ("Corteva") including Corteva's subsidiary EIDP, (the "Corteva Distribution" and together with the Dow Distribution, the "DWDP Distributions").
On its transformation journey from a specialty products company to a focused advanced solutions provider, DuPont has taken the following actions:
•the divestiture in 2021 of the Nutrition & Biosciences ("N&B") business to International Flavors & Fragrance Inc. ("IFF") in a Reverse Morris Trust transaction (the "N&B Transaction");
•the divestiture in 2022 of the majority of the businesses comprising the historical Materials & Mobility (M&M) segment to Celanese Corporation (the "M&M Divestiture");

•the divestiture in 2023 of the Delrin® business, part of the historical M&M segment, to TJC LP ("TJC"), (the "Delrin® Divestiture" and together with the M&M Divestiture, referred to as the "M&M Divestitures");

•the entry in the third quarter of 2025 into a definitive agreement to sell the Aramids business (the "Aramids Divestiture") to Arclin, a portfolio company of an affiliate of TJC, in a transaction that is expected to close around the end of the first quarter 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and receipt of regulatory approvals; and

•the separation of its semiconductor and interconnect solutions businesses, (the "Electronics Business" and the separation of the Electronics Business, the "Electronics Separation") into an independent public company, Qnity Electronics, Inc. ("Qnity"), by way of the distribution to DuPont's stockholders of record as of October 22, 2025 of all the issued and outstanding common stock of Qnity on November 1, 2025 (the "Qnity Distribution").
See Part II, Item 7 Management's Discussion & Analysis and Notes 4 and 15 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for more information.

The M&M Divestitures, intended Aramids Divestiture, and Electronics Separation represent strategic shifts with related major impacts on DuPont's operations and results. The revenues and certain expenses of the M&M Businesses, Aramids Business, and Electronics Business are classified as discontinued operations in the current and historical periods.

The Consolidated Financial Statements included in this annual report present the financial position of DuPont as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the results of operations of DuPont for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, and the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows giving effect to the M&M Divestitures, Aramids Divestiture, and Electronics Separation as if each had occurred on January 1, 2023, with the historical financial results of the businesses divested as part of the aforementioned divestitures (the "M&M Businesses", "Aramids Business", and "Electronics Business") reflected as discontinued operations, as applicable. The comprehensive income related to the M&M Businesses, Aramids Business, and Electronics Business has not been segregated and is included in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income, for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, as applicable. Unless otherwise indicated, the information in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements refer only to DuPont's continuing operations and do not include discussion of balances or activity of discontinued operations.

Effective in the fourth quarter of 2025, following the Electronics Separation, the Company realigned its management and reporting structure. This realignment resulted in a change in reportable segments which changed the manner in which the Company reports its financial results (the "Q4 2025 Segment Realignment"), creating two new reportable segments: Healthcare & Water Technologies and Diversified Industrials. headings: Risks Relating to the Qnity Distribution, M&M Divestitures, N&B Transaction, the DWDP Distributions and the Aramids Divestiture
The separation and combination of DuPont's Nutrition & Biosciences business with IFF could result in a significant tax liability to DuPont.
DuPont is subject to continuing contingent tax-related liabilities of Dow and Corteva following the DWDP Distributions.
The timing and outcome of the Aramids Divestiture is subject to risk and uncertainties.
Risks Relating to DuPont's Business and Results of Operations
An impairment of goodwill or intangible assets could negatively impact the Company's financial results.

Failure to effectively manage acquisitions, divestitures, alliances and other portfolio actions could adversely impact the Company's business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
The Company's results are affected by its ability to foresee and respond to competitive conditions and customer preferences.
Failure to attract and retain talented people with the necessary knowledge and experience could adversely affect Company's ability to compete and achieve its strategic goals.
Risks Relating to Capital Resources and Liquidity
A significant percentage of the Company's net sales are generated from the Company's international operations and are subject to economic, geo-political, foreign exchange and other risks.
Risks Related to Regulatory Changes and Compliance
The Company's business, results of operations and reputation could be adversely affected by industry-specific risks including process safety and product stewardship/regulatory compliance issues.
paragraphs: The Company's operations could be affected by various risks, many of which are beyond its control. Based on current information, the Company believes that the following identifies the most material risk factors that could affect its operations. Past financial performance may not be a reliable indicator of future performance and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods.

If the Qnity Distribution, together with certain related transactions, including the cash distribution Qnity made to DuPont prior to the Qnity Distribution, were to fail to qualify for non-recognition treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes, then DuPont could be subject to significant tax liability.

DuPont received an opinion of counsel as a condition to the Qnity Distribution, in form and substance acceptable to DuPont, substantially to the effect that, among other things, the Qnity Distribution along with certain related transactions will qualify for non-recognition treatment under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code", and such opinion, the "Tax Opinion"). The Tax Opinion relied on certain facts, assumptions, and undertakings, and certain representations from DuPont and Qnity, regarding the past and future conduct of each of their respective businesses and other matters. Notwithstanding the receipt of the Tax Opinion, the Internal Revenue Service (the "IRS") could determine on audit that the Qnity Distribution and/or certain related transactions should be treated as taxable transactions if it determines that any of these facts, assumptions, representations or undertakings are not correct or have been violated, or that the Qnity Distribution should be taxable for other reasons, including if the IRS were to disagree with the conclusions of the Tax Opinion. If the Qnity Distribution and/or certain related transactions fail to qualify for tax-free treatment under U.S. federal, state and local tax law and/or foreign tax law, it is expected that DuPont could incur significant tax liabilities under U.S. federal, state, local and/or foreign tax law.

Generally, corporate taxes resulting from the failure of the Qnity Distribution to qualify for tax-free treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes would be imposed on DuPont. Under the Tax Matters Agreement, effective as of November 1, 2025, between DuPont and Qnity (the "Electronics Tax Matters Agreement"), the responsibility for such taxes may be allocated between DuPont and Qnity under certain circumstances and each of DuPont and Qnity may be obligated to indemnify the other against any such taxes imposed on it. To the extent that DuPont is responsible for any liability as a result of the failure of the Qnity Distribution and/or certain related transactions to qualify for non-recognition treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes, there could be a material adverse impact on DuPont's business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows in subsequent reporting periods.

DuPont could incur additional tax liabilities if certain internal transactions undertaken in connection with the completed divestiture of a majority of the Mobility & Materials business to Celanese and divestiture of the Delrin® business to TJC (the "M&M Divestitures"), fail to qualify for their intended tax treatment.

Prior to the closing of the M&M Divestitures, DuPont engaged in certain internal reorganization activities to separate into and to separately align the legal entities holding the M&M Business and the Delrin® business for disposition. DuPont has recognized a tax liability pursuant to these reorganization activities related to the M&M Divestitures. However, if certain of these internal reorganization activities fail to qualify for their intended tax treatment under U.S. federal, state, local tax and/or foreign tax law, DuPont could incur additional tax liabilities. Pursuant to the Electronics Tax Matters Agreement, any such additional tax liabilities incurred by DuPont (if any) will be contractually allocated between DuPont and Qnity generally based on their respective Applicable Percentage, as defined in the Separation and Distribution Agreement, effective as of November 1, 2025, between DuPont and Qnity (the "Electronics Separation and Distribution Agreement"). The Applicable Percentage for DuPont is 56 percent and for Qnity is 44 percent.

Components of management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations include:
•Overview •Analysis of Operations •Result of Operations •Segment Results •Outlook •Liquidity and Capital Resources
•Recent Accounting Pronouncements •Critical Accounting Estimates •Long-Term Employee Benefits

As of December 31, 2025, the Company has $1.7 billion of net working capital and $0.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents. The Company expects its cash and cash equivalents, cash generated from operations, and ability to access the debt capital markets to provide sufficient liquidity and financial flexibility to meet the liquidity requirements associated with its continued operations. The Company continually assesses its liquidity position, including possible sources of incremental liquidity, in light of the current economic environment, capital market conditions and Company performance.

On November 1, 2025, the Company completed the separation of its semiconductor and interconnect solutions businesses, (the "Electronics Business" and the separation of the Electronics Business, the "Electronics Separation") into an independent public company, Qnity Electronics, Inc. ("Qnity"), by way of the distribution to DuPont's stockholders of record as of October 22, 2025, of all the issued and outstanding common stock of Qnity on November 1, 2025 (the "Qnity Distribution"). As a result, the financial results of the divested Electronics Business are reflected in DuPont's Consolidated Financial Statements as discontinued operations, along with comparative periods.

On August 29, 2025, DuPont announced a definitive agreement to sell the Aramids business (the "Aramids Divestiture") to Arclin, a portfolio company of an affiliate of TJC LP, ("TJC"), in return for pre-tax cash proceeds of approximately $1.2 billion, subject to customary transaction adjustments, a note receivable in the principal amount of $300 million and a non-controlling common equity interest (the "Aramids Equity Consideration"), valued at $325 million in the future Arclin holding company that will hold the Arclin global materials business and the Aramids business being divested. The transaction is expected to close around the end of the first quarter 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and receipt of regulatory approvals. As a result, the financial results of the Aramids business being divested are reflected in DuPont's Consolidated Financial Statements as discontinued operations, along with comparative periods.

Effective in the first quarter of 2025, in preparation for the Electronics Separation, the Company realigned its management and reporting structure. This realignment resulted in a change in reportable segments in the first quarter of 2025 which changed the manner in which the Company reported financial results by segment, (the "Q1 2025 Segment Realignment"). As a result, starting in the first quarter of 2025 and until the Electronics Separation, the businesses separated as part of the Electronics Separation were reported separately from the Industrials businesses of DuPont.

Effective in the fourth quarter of 2025, following the Electronics Separation, the Company realigned its management and reporting structure. This realignment resulted in a change in reportable segments which changed the manner in which the Company reports its financial results (the "Q4 2025 Segment Realignment"), creating two new reportable segments: Healthcare & Water Technologies and Diversified Industrials. The results of operations discussion included in Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, as well as the segment information in the Consolidated Financial Statements, are reflective of the impact of the Q4 2025 Segment Realignment and reflect the two segment reporting structure for all periods presented.

On November 1, 2022, DuPont completed the previously announced divestiture of the majority of the historical Mobility & Materials segment, including the Engineering Polymers business line and select product lines within the Advanced Solutions and Performance Resins business lines (the "M&M Divestiture"). On February 18, 2022, the Company announced that its Board of Directors approved of the divestiture of the Delrin® acetal homopolymer (H-POM) business (the "Delrin® Divestiture"). On November 1, 2023, the Company closed the sale of the Delrin® business to TJC LP ("TJC"), (the "Delrin® Divestiture"). DuPont received cash proceeds of approximately $1.28 billion, which includes certain customary transaction adjustments, a note receivable of $350 million and acquired a 19.9 percent noncontrolling equity interest in Derby Group Holdings LLC, ("Derby"). The customary transaction adjustments related to $27 million of cash transferred with the Delrin® Divestiture for which DuPont was reimbursed at closing resulting in net cash proceeds of $1.25 billion. TJC, through its subsidiaries, holds the 80.1 percent controlling interest in Derby. The Delrin® Divestiture together with the divestiture of the majority of the historic Mobility & Materials segment in 2022 (collectively the "M&M Divestitures" and the businesses in scope for the M&M Divestitures collectively the "M&M Businesses") represent a strategic shift that has a major impact on DuPont's operations and results.

The M&M Divestitures, Aramids Divestiture, and Electronics Separation represent strategic shifts with related major impacts on DuPont's operations and results and are reported as discontinued operations.

The Consolidated Financial Statements present the financial position of DuPont as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the results of operations of DuPont for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, and the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows giving effect to the M&M Divestiture, Aramids Divestiture, and Electronics Separation as if each had occurred on January 1, 2023, with the historical financial results of the businesses divested as part of the aforementioned divestitures (the "M&M Businesses", "Aramids Business", and "Electronics Business") reflected as discontinued operations, as applicable. The comprehensive income related to the M&M Businesses, Aramids Business, and Electronics Business has not been segregated and are included in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income, for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, as applicable. Unless otherwise indicated, the information in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements refer only to DuPont's continuing operations and do not include discussion of balances or activity of discontinued operations

On October 10, 2025, DuPont completed the acquisition of Sinochem (Ningbo) RO Memtech Co., Ltd. ("Sinochem") for a net purchase price of $56 million (the "Sinochem Acquisition"). Sinochem is a reverse osmosis manufacturer located in China and the Asia Pacific region. Sinochem is part of Water Technologies within the Healthcare & Water Technologies segment. See Note 3 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information.

On July 28, 2024, DuPont completed the acquisition of Donatelle Plastics, LLC ("Donatelle"), for a net purchase price of $365 million (the "Donatelle Acquisition") which includes immaterial adjustments for acquired cash and net working capital. The net purchase price also included the estimated fair value for a contingent earn-out liability of $40 million. Donatelle is a medical device company specializing in the design, development and manufacture of medical components and devices. Donatelle is part of Healthcare Technologies within the Healthcare & Water Technologies segment. See Note 3 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information.

On August 1, 2023, the Company completed the acquisition of Spectrum Plastics Group ("Spectrum") from AEA Investors (the "Spectrum Acquisition"). Spectrum manufactures flexible packaging products, plastic and silicone extrusions, and components for the industrial, food and medical business sectors throughout the United States and international markets. Spectrum is primarily reported in the Healthcare Technologies business within the Healthcare & Water Technologies segment. The net purchase price was approximately $1,781 million, including a net upward adjustment of approximately $43 million for acquired cash and net working capital, among other items. See Note 3 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information.
本年度10-K形式年度報告中，除非上下文另有說明， herein所使用的"DuPont"或"Company"一詞均指DuPont de Nemours, Inc.及其合併子公司。

DuPont為提供先進解決方案的領導者，這些解決方案改善人們在醫療、水、建設與工業市場的日常生活。本公司致力於協助客戶推進其技術管道，並提供解決其獨特挑戰的方案。從提供乾淨的水到啟動醫療包裝方案以提升安全與性能，DuPont的創新驅動人們日常依賴的基礎產品與技術。截至2025年12月31日，本公司在全球約50個國家設有子公司，並在約20個國家進行製造業務。有關本公司銷售與財產所在地點的詳細資訊，請參閱財務會計彙編財務資料附註23。

DuPont為於2015年成立的德拉瓦州公司（原為DowDuPont Inc.），其成立目的為執行The Dow Chemical Company（"TDCC"）與E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company（n/k/a as EIDP, Inc., "EIDP"）之間的全股票合併交易，該交易於2017年8月31日生效。根據該合併，TDCC與EIDP成為DowDuPont Inc.的子公司（"DWDP合併"）。DWDP合併旨在結合兩家公司之優勢，並重新配置資產以創造三個更專注且簡化之公開上市公司。
於2019年4月1日，本公司透過分拆Dow Inc.（"Dow"）完成材料科學業務的分離，包括Dow的子公司TDCC（"Dow分拆"）。於2019年6月1日，本公司透過分拆Corteva, Inc.（"Corteva"）完成農業業務的分離，包括Corteva的子公司EIDP（"Corteva分拆"，與Dow分拆合稱"DWDP分拆"）。
在從專門產品公司轉型為專注先進解決方案供應商的旅程中，DuPont已採取以下行動：
•於2021年透過反向莫里斯信託交易（"N&B交易"）將Nutrition & Biosciences（"N&B"）業務出售給International Flavors & Fragrance Inc.（"IFF"）；
•於2022年將歷史Materials & Mobility（M&M）業務的大多數部分出售給Celanese Corporation（"M&M出售"）；
•於2023年將Delrin®業務（為歷史M&M業務的一部分）出售給TJC LP（"TJC"）（"Delrin®出售"，與M&M出售合稱"M&M出售"）；
•於2025年第三季進入與Aramid商務（"Aramid資產出售"）簽訂最終協議，出售予Aclin，為TJC之附屬公司之投資組合公司，預期於2026年第一季末完成交易，依慣例完成條件及取得監管機構批准為前提；及
•將其半導體及連接解決方案商務（"電子商務"及"電子商務分離"）分離為獨立上市公司Qnity Electronics, Inc.（"Qnity"），透過於2025年10月22日為登記股東之杜邦股東，於2025年11月1日發放所有已發行及流通之Qnity普通股（"Qnity分發"）。
請參閱第二部分，第7項管理層討論與分析及合併財務明細表之附註4及15以取得更多資訊。
M&M資產出售、預期Aramid資產出售及電子商務分離代表戰略轉變，並對杜邦之營運及結果產生相關重大影響。M&M商務、Aramid商務及電子商務之收入及部分費用於目前及歷史期間被歸類為已終止營運。

本年度報告所包含之合併財務明細表，呈現杜邦於2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日之財務狀況，杜邦於2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之營運結果，以及考慮M&M資產出售、Aramid資產出售及電子商務分離後之現金流量明細表，如同各項交易於2023年1月1日即已發生，並反映上述資產出售之歷史財務結果（"M&M商務"、"Aramid商務"及"電子商務"）作為已終止營運，如適用。M&M商務、Aramid商務及電子商務之綜合損益未經分離，並包含於合併綜合損益明細表中，於2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之營運結果，如適用。除非另有說明，合併財務明細表之附註資訊僅指杜邦持續營運，不包含已終止營運之餘額或活動之討論。
自2025年第四季起，於電子商務分離後，本公司重新調整其管理與報告結構。此調整導致報告分部之變更，改變本公司報告財務結果之方式（"2025年第四季分部調整"），創造兩個新報告分部：醫療與水科技及多元化工業。因此，合併財務明細表已重新整理，以反映上述兩分部報告結構，如下所述：

paragraphs: 管理階層對於財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，作為財務報表之補充資料，應與合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀，以增進對本公司營運及現行商業環境之理解。管理階層對於財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析之內容包括：
•總覽 •營運分析 •營運成果 •分部成果 •展望 •流動性與資本運用
•近期會計準則更新 •關鍵會計估計 •長期員工福利
截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有淨營運資金17億美元，現金及現金等價物為7億美元。本公司預期其現金及現金等價物、營運活動所產生之現金，以及取得負債資本市場之能力，將提供足夠之流動性與財務彈性，以應付持續營運所產生之流動性需求。本公司持續評估其流動性狀況，包括可能之額外流動性來源，並考量目前經濟環境、資本市場條件及本公司營運表現。

2025年11月1日，本公司完成將半導體與連接解決方案業務（稱為「電子業務」，以及分離電子業務之程序，稱為「電子業務分離」）分離，成立獨立上市之公司Qnity Electronics, Inc.（「Qnity」），透過於2025年10月22日登記為杜邦股東之股東，於2025年11月1日發放所有Qnity已發行且流通之普通股（稱為「Qnity分發」）。因此，已分離之電子業務之財務結果，反映在杜邦合併財務報表中作為已終止營運，並包含比較期間。

2025年8月29日，杜邦宣佈與Arclin簽訂最終協議，將纖維素業務（稱為「纖維素業務出售」）出售給Arclin，為TJC LP之附屬公司之投資組合公司（「TJC」），以換取預稅現金約12億美元，扣除常見交易調整後，一筆本金為3億美元之應收款，以及一項非控制性普通股權益（稱為「纖維素權益對價」），價值約3.25億美元，此價值為未來將持有纖維素全球材料業務與被出售之纖維素業務之Arclin控股公司。交易預計於2026年第一季末完成，視常見關閉條件及取得監管批准而定。因此，被出售之纖維素業務之財務結果，反映在杜邦合併財務報表中作為已終止營運，並包含比較期間。
自2025年第一季起，為準備電子業務分離，本公司重新調整其管理與報告結構。此調整導致2025年第一季報告分部之變更，改變本公司按分部報告財務結果之方式（稱為「2025年第一季分部調整」）。因此，自2025年第一季起至電子業務分離完成為止，分離之業務已獨立於杜邦之工業業務進行報告。
自2025年第四季起，電子業務分離後，本公司重新調整其管理與報告結構。此調整導致報告分部之變更，改變本公司報告財務結果之方式（稱為「2025年第四季分部調整」），創造兩個新的報告分部：醫療與水科技及多元化工業。管理階層對於財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，以及合併財務報表中之分部資訊，反映2025年第四季分部調整之影響，並反映所有期間之兩分部報告結構。

於2022年11月1日，杜邦完成先前宣佈的將歷史性移動與材料分部的大多數業務，包括工程塑料業務線及先進解決方案與性能樹脂業務線中的選定產品線（稱為"M&M 資產出售"）的出售。於2022年2月18日，本公司宣佈其董事會批准出售Delrin® 醋酸均聚物（H-POM）業務（稱為"Delrin® 資產出售"）。於2023年11月1日，本公司完成將Delrin® 業務出售給TJC LP（"TJC"）（稱為"Delrin® 資產出售"）。杜邦收到約12.8億美元現金，包含某些慣例交易調整、3.5億美元應收款及取得Derby Group Holdings LLC（"Derby"）19.9％非控制性權益。慣例交易調整涉及因Delrin® 資產出售而轉移2700萬美元現金，杜邦在交易關閉時獲得補償，因此淨現金收入為125億美元。TJC透過其子公司持有Derby 80.1％控制性權益。Delrin® 資產出售與2022年出售歷史性移動與材料分部的大多數業務（合稱"M&M 資產出售"）代表一項戰略轉變，對杜邦的營運與結果產生重大影響。
M&M 資產出售、Aramids 資產出售及電子業務分離代表戰略轉變，對杜邦的營運與結果產生相關重大影響，並被列為已終止營運業務。

合併財務報表呈現杜邦截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日的財務狀況，以及杜邦截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日的營運結果，以及考慮M&M 資產出售、Aramids 資產出售及電子業務分離後的現金流量表，如同這些交易均於2023年1月1日發生，已出售業務的歷史財務結果（稱為"M&M 事業"、"Aramids 事業"及"電子業務"）已列為已終止營運業務，如適用。M&M 事業、Aramids 事業及電子業務的綜合損益未經分離，並包含於合併綜合損益表中，截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日，如適用。除非另有說明，財務報表附註所提及資訊僅針對杜邦持續營運業務，不包含已終止營運業務的餘額或活動討論。
於2025年10月10日，杜邦完成對Sinochem (Ningbo) RO Memtech Co., Ltd.（"Sinochem"）的收購，淨購價為5600萬美元（稱為"Sinochem 收購"）。Sinochem 是位於中國及亞太地區的反滲透製造商。Sinochem 屬於水科技，為醫療與水科技分部的一部分。詳見合併財務報表附註3以取得更多資訊。

於2024年7月28日，杜邦完成對Donatelle Plastics, LLC（"Donatelle"）的收購，淨購價為3.65億美元（稱為"Donatelle 收購"），包含對取得現金及淨營運資金的微小調整。淨購價亦包含對應 contingent earn-out 應付義務的預估公允價值4000萬美元。Donatelle 是一家醫療器材公司，專門從事醫療組件及設備的設計、開發與製造。Donatelle 屬於醫療科技，為醫療與水科技分部的一部分。詳見合併財務報表附註3以取得更多資訊。

於2023年8月1日，本公司完成從AEA Investors（"AEA Investors"）購入Spectrum Plastics Group（"Spectrum"）（稱為"Spectrum 收購"）。Spectrum 生產柔性的包裝產品、塑膠及矽膠擠出產品，以及工業、食品及醫療業務領域的零組件，遍及美國及國際市場。Spectrum 主要歸屬於醫療科技，為醫療與水科技分部的一部分。淨購價約為17.81億美元，包含對取得現金及淨營運資金的淨上調約4300萬美元，及其他項目。詳見合併財務報表附註3以取得更多資訊。

headings: 與 Qnity 分銷、M&M 資產處分、N&B 交易、DWDP 分紅及 Aramids 資產處分相關之風險
杜邦公司與 IFF 之間的營養與生物科技業務分拆與合併，可能會導致杜邦公司產生重大稅務負擔。
杜邦公司於 DWDP 分紅後，仍可能面臨持續性的與稅務相關之或有負債，該負債源自於 Dow 及 Corteva。
Aramids 資產處分之時程與結果，存在風險與不確定性。
與杜邦公司業務及營運成果相關之風險
商譽或無形資產之減損，可能對本公司之財務成果造成負面影響。
若無法有效管理併購、資產處分、合作夥伴關係及其他資產組合行動，可能對本公司之業務、營運成果、財務狀況及現金流造成不利影響。
本公司之營運成果受其預測並回應競爭環境與客戶偏好之能力所影響。
未能吸引並留住具備必要知識與經驗的人才，可能會不利於本公司競爭能力及達成其戰略目標。
與資本資源及流動性相關的風險
本公司淨銷售額的相當大比例來自國際業務，並受經濟、地緣政治、外匯及其他風險影響。
與法規變更及合規相關的風險
本公司業務、營運成果及聲譽可能因產業特定風險而受到不利影響，包括製程安全及產品責任/法規合規問題。
paragraphs: 本公司的營運可能受到多種風險影響，其中許多風險超出本公司控制範圍。根據現有資訊，本公司認為下列內容為最重大可能影響其營運的風險因素。過去的財務表現未必能作為未來表現的可靠指標，歷史趨勢亦不應用以預測未來期間的結果或趨勢。
若 Qnity Distribution 連同某些相關交易，包括 Qnity 發給杜邦的現金分紅，未能符合美國聯邦所得稅目的的非認列待遇，則杜邦可能面臨重大稅務負擔。

杜邦為 Qnity Distribution 而取得律師意見，該意見形式與內容均符合杜邦接受的標準，內容大致為：在1986年內政部稅法（Internal Revenue Code of 1986，經修正）下，Qnity Distribution 連同某些相關交易將符合非認列待遇（"Code"，此意見稱為 "Tax Opinion"）。此 Tax Opinion 依賴某些事實、假設、承諾，以及杜邦與 Qnity 所提供的有關各自業務過去與未來行為及其他事項的陳述。即使取得 Tax Opinion，美國國稅局（IRS）仍可能在稽查時判定 Qnity Distribution 以及某些相關交易應被視為課稅交易，若 IRS 判斷上述任何事實、假設、陳述或承諾不正確或已被違反，或 Qnity Distribution 因其他原因應被課稅，包括 IRS 與 Tax Opinion 的結論意見不一致。若 Qnity Distribution 以及某些相關交易未能符合美國聯邦、州、地方及/或外國稅法下的稅務豁免待遇，預期杜邦可能根據美國聯邦、州、地方及/或外國稅法承擔重大稅務負擔。

若 Qnity Distribution 未能符合美國聯邦所得稅目的的稅務豁免待遇，則杜邦將需承擔因該失敗而產生的公司稅。根據於2025年11月1日生效的杜邦與 Qnity 之間的稅務事務協議（"Electronics Tax Matters Agreement"），在特定情況下，此稅務責任可能在杜邦與 Qnity 之間分配，且杜邦與 Qnity 均可能需對對方因此稅務責任而產生的損失進行賠償。若杜邦因 Qnity Distribution 以及/或某些相關交易未能符合美國聯邦所得稅目的的非認列待遇而承擔任何責任，則可能對杜邦未來會計期間的營運、財務狀況、營業成果及現金流產生重大不利影響。
若與已完成將大多數 Mobility & Materials 事業出售給 Celanese 以及將 Delrin® 事業出售給 TJC（"M&M Divestitures"）相關的某些內部交易未能符合其預期的稅務待遇，杜邦可能需承擔額外稅務負擔。

在 M&M Divestitures 交易完成前，杜邦進行某些內部重整活動，以分離並獨立對應持有 M&M 事業與 Delrin® 事業的法律實體，以便進行處分。杜邦已根據這些重整活動認列與 M&M Divestitures 相關的稅務負擔。然而，若某些這些內部重整活動未能符合其預期的稅務待遇，根據美國聯邦、州、地方及/或外國稅法，杜邦可能需承擔額外稅務負擔。根據 Electronics Tax Matters Agreement，杜邦所承擔的任何額外稅務負擔（如有）將根據杜邦與 Qnity 之間於2025年11月1日生效的 Separation and Distribution Agreement 所定義的 Applicable Percentage 進行契約分配。杜邦的 Applicable Percentage 為 56%，Qnity 為 44%。
